activity_label.en: Combating corruption (A9-0048/2024 - Raquel García Hermida-Van Der Walle)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Cristian Terheş (ECR).

Madam President, I voted against the Anti-Corruption Directive because it violates fundamental European values that made the EU different from the Soviet Union in the past.

1. The Directive interferes with competences belonging to the Member States, in breach of national sovereignty and the principle of subsidiarity.

2. Certain crimes are defined vaguely or even absurdly, which creates serious risks of abuse, which has already been reported by NGOs. For example, articles on bribery and influence peddling criminalise the mere promise to take unfair advantage of a public official, even if that promise is not followed by either the giving of benefits or any concrete action by the public official. Basically, words not followed by any deed are incriminated, which is absurd. It is also here that improper influence on the official is criminalized, without defining which influence is proper and which is improper.

The Directive also imposes obligations on Member States, but exempts the EU institutions from binding transparency rules.

In short, the EU legislates for others, while Ursula will be able to continue and exercise her discretionary power without being sanctioned.

activity_label.en: Global Gateway – past impacts and future orientation (A10-0045/2026 - Chloé Ridel, Hildegard Bentele)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Cristian Terheş (ECR).

Madam President, I voted in favour of the Global Gateway report from geopolitical realism.

To count on the world stage, the EU must abandon its role as an actor, which only regulates and gives lessons to others, and invest in infrastructure. While the EU was teaching different countries how to regulate that men can give birth, China, through the Belt and Road Initiative, invested billions of euros in digital transport and energy infrastructure.

Europe cannot afford the luxury of naivety or passivity. If we do not offer an alternative to these countries, they will not run out of infrastructure, if we do not get involved, other countries will.

Global Gateway is right because it protects concrete European interests – access to critical raw materials and secure trade routes. It is fundamental to diversify trade routes and reduce dependencies. Connecting with Central Asia and Development Middle Corridor must become clear priorities.

At the same time, Global Gateway must not become a vehicle to advance the ideological agenda of the European Commission. It needs to be invested in infrastructure, not social engineering. Invested in partnerships, not political conditioning. Europeans' money must serve Europe's interests, not the experiments of bureaucrats.

activity_label.en: Global Gateway – past impacts and future orientation (debate)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Tomasz Froelich (ESN), written

The world order is becoming multipolar. That can be welcomed. That can be rejected. But that is a fact. In this multipolar world order there is a struggle for influence. To raw materials. To good trade relations. To infrastructure. To connectivity. We Europeans have lost a lot of influence worldwide in recent decades. Our share of global GDP is gradually falling. Our importance is diminishing. Other China: Beijing's economy is booming. Beijing's influence is growing. In Asia, in Africa, everywhere. This is closely linked to the New Silk Road project, which can also be an opportunity for us. This does not mean that we should not use our own geostrategic instruments in global competition, including in the area of development policy. Global Gateway could be one such tool. Could, but it isn't. Because it is completely wrongly conceived: Instead of using Global Gateway to expand infrastructure projects in third countries, secure access to resources and create win-win situations in international trade, this project is being misused for woken values imperialism, arrogant teachings and climate goals that make the rich poor and the poorest even poorer – at the price of EUR 300 billion so far, which has been spent intransparently. That doesn't help us. This only hurts us – and makes Europe increasingly unpopular and irrelevant around the world. Stop it! We really need more China in development policy.
